Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural science can be defined as the
options: science and art of crop and livestock production, processing and marketing for man's use
rearing of animals for sport only
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: science and art of crop and livestock production, processing and marketing for man's use

Basic Concepts.text: Which of the following is a branch of agricultural science concerned with soil study?
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Pedology

Basic Concepts.text: The branch of agriculture dealing with breeding, feeding and management of livestock is
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Animal science

Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural science is important to the individual mainly because it
options: has no benefit to an individual
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: provides food, employment and income

Basic Concepts.text: Agriculture contributes to community development mainly through
options: provision of employment and raw materials for local industries
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: provision of employment and raw materials for local industries

Basic Concepts.text: At the national level, agriculture contributes to development mainly by
options: earning foreign exchange and providing raw materials for industries
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: earning foreign exchange and providing raw materials for industries

Basic Concepts.text: Pomology is the branch of agriculture concerned with
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: fruit production

Basic Concepts.text: Olericulture deals with the cultivation of
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: vegetables

Basic Concepts.text: The study of insects, including those affecting crops, is called
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Entomology

Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural economics deals mainly with
options: the efficient allocation of scarce resources in agricultural production
the breeding of new crop varieties
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: the efficient allocation of scarce resources in agricultural production

Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural extension is the branch of agriculture concerned with
options: educating farmers on improved farming practices
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: educating farmers on improved farming practices

Basic Concepts.text: Which of these best describes the importance of agriculture in providing raw materials?
options: Crude oil for the petroleum industry
Iron ore for the steel industry
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Cotton for the textile industry

Basic Concepts.text: Agriculture provides employment mainly for the population living in
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: rural areas of developing countries

Basic Concepts.text: Agriculture serves as a source of foreign exchange earnings through
options: export of cash crops such as cocoa and rubber
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: export of cash crops such as cocoa and rubber

Basic Concepts.text: Which of the following best illustrates agriculture's contribution to national food security?
options: Ensuring adequate and steady food supply for the population
Encouraging total dependence on food imports
Reducing local crop production Page 4 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Ensuring adequate and steady food supply for the population

Basic Concepts.text: A major problem affecting agricultural development related to land is
options: insecure land tenure systems limiting access
abundant unrestricted land for every farmer
excess land title documentation for all farmers
absence of any customary land practice
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: insecure land tenure systems limiting access

Basic Concepts.text: Poor rural infrastructure such as roads is a problem because it
options: increases the cost and difficulty of moving farm produce to market
reduces the cost of transporting produce
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: increases the cost and difficulty of moving farm produce to market

Basic Concepts.text: Inadequate finance is a major constraint to agricultural development because farmers
options: cannot afford improved inputs and equipment
have excess capital with no use for it
do not require capital to farm
can always access unlimited free credit
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: cannot afford improved inputs and equipment

Basic Concepts.text: Poor transportation facilities affect agriculture mainly by
options: increasing post-harvest losses and delaying produce to market
reducing the cost of moving produce
having no bearing on farm produce
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: increasing post-harvest losses and delaying produce to market

Basic Concepts.text: Inadequate storage and processing facilities lead to
options: high post-harvest losses of perishable produce
no effect on farm produce value
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: high post-harvest losses of perishable produce

Basic Concepts.text: A lack of adequate agricultural education and extension services results in
options: slow adoption of improved farming techniques by farmers
rapid and complete adoption of all new techniques
elimination of the need for research
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: slow adoption of improved farming techniques by farmers

Basic Concepts.text: Inadequate farm tools and machinery is a problem because it
options: limits the scale and efficiency of farm operations
has no bearing on farm output
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: limits the scale and efficiency of farm operations

Basic Concepts.text: High cost of farm inputs such as fertilizer and seeds is a challenge because it
options: reduces farmers' ability to purchase adequate inputs
is not a factor in production decisions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: reduces farmers' ability to purchase adequate inputs

Basic Concepts.text: A poor marketing system negatively affects farmers by
options: causing low prices for produce due to exploitation by middlemen
guaranteeing farmers the highest possible prices always
having no effect on farm income
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: causing low prices for produce due to exploitation by middlemen

Basic Concepts.text: Environmental degradation such as soil erosion and desertification is a challenge to agriculture because it
options: reduces the productive capacity of farmland
has no long-term effect on farming
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: reduces the productive capacity of farmland

Basic Concepts.text: A possible solution to the problem of land tenure insecurity is
options: land reforms such as the Land Use Act to improve access
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: land reforms such as the Land Use Act to improve access

Basic Concepts.text: A possible solution to the problem of inadequate finance for farmers is
options: provision of agricultural credit facilities and subsidies
denial of all forms of credit
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: provision of agricultural credit facilities and subsidies

Basic Concepts.text: A possible solution to poor transportation in rural farming areas is
options: construction and maintenance of rural feeder roads
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: construction and maintenance of rural feeder roads

Basic Concepts.text: Establishing agricultural extension services helps solve the problem of
options: farmers' limited access to improved knowledge and practices
absence of any need for farmer training
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: farmers' limited access to improved knowledge and practices

Basic Concepts.text: Provision of storage facilities like silos and warehouses helps to solve the problem of
options: excess crop production Page 6 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: post-harvest losses

Basic Concepts.text: Subsistence agriculture is best described as farming carried out mainly for
options: family/household consumption with little surplus for sale
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: family/household consumption with little surplus for sale

Basic Concepts.text: Commercial agriculture is characterized mainly by
options: large-scale production primarily for sale and profit
use of only traditional hand tools
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: large-scale production primarily for sale and profit

Basic Concepts.text: One key difference between subsistence and commercial agriculture is that commercial agriculture
options: involves large farm size and higher input use
always involves smaller farm size than subsistence
is practiced only by families for their own food
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: involves large farm size and higher input use

Basic Concepts.text: An advantage of subsistence agriculture is that it
options: provides food security directly for the farming household
always generates high profit for export
is the dominant form of agriculture in industrialized nations
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: provides food security directly for the farming household

Basic Concepts.text: A disadvantage of subsistence agriculture is
options: low output due to limited use of modern inputs and small farm size
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: low output due to limited use of modern inputs and small farm size

Basic Concepts.text: An advantage of commercial agriculture is
options: higher output and income due to economies of scale
total reliance on manual labour only
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: higher output and income due to economies of scale

Basic Concepts.text: A disadvantage of commercial agriculture is that it
options: requires substantial capital investment which may be difficult to raise
always leads to reduced yield Page 7 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
is unaffected by market price fluctuations
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: requires substantial capital investment which may be difficult to raise

Basic Concepts.text: A common problem of subsistence farming is
options: low productivity due to reliance on traditional methods
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: low productivity due to reliance on traditional methods

Basic Concepts.text: A common problem of commercial farming in West Africa includes
options: high cost of inputs and access to credit
total absence of any market for produce
excess and cheap access to unlimited capital
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: high cost of inputs and access to credit

Basic Concepts.text: Which of these is a characteristic feature distinguishing commercial from subsistence agriculture?
options: Level of mechanization and market orientation
The type of crop grown, since only commercial farms grow crops
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Level of mechanization and market orientation

Basic Concepts.text: Government provides agricultural credit to farmers mainly to
options: increase farmers' access to capital for production
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: increase farmers' access to capital for production

Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural subsidies granted by government are intended to
options: reduce the cost of farm inputs to farmers
increase the cost of farm inputs
discourage the use of improved inputs
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: reduce the cost of farm inputs to farmers

Basic Concepts.text: Government involvement in agricultural education is important mainly to
options: train skilled manpower for the agricultural sector
reduce the number of agricultural graduates
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: train skilled manpower for the agricultural sector

Basic Concepts.text: Government agricultural extension services help farmers mainly by
options: providing technical advice and improved farming techniques
reducing crop yield Page 8 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: providing technical advice and improved farming techniques

Basic Concepts.text: Agricultural policies formulated by government are aimed at
options: promoting increased and sustainable agricultural production
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: promoting increased and sustainable agricultural production

Basic Concepts.text: Which of these is an example of a government agricultural programme in West Africa?
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Operation Feed the Nation (OFN)

Basic Concepts.text: The Agricultural Development Programme (ADP) was established mainly to
options: provide integrated support (inputs, extension, credit) to farmers
discourage rural farmers from producing food
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: provide integrated support (inputs, extension, credit) to farmers

Basic Concepts.text: Farm Settlement schemes established by some West African governments aimed to
options: resettle and train young farmers on organized farm land with modern methods
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: resettle and train young farmers on organized farm land with modern methods

Basic Concepts.text: The Agricultural Sector Rehabilitation Project (ASRP) was designed mainly to
options: rehabilitate and revamp the agricultural sector through investment and reform
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: rehabilitate and revamp the agricultural sector through investment and reform

Basic Concepts.text: Government fiscal policies such as import restrictions on certain food items are aimed at
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: protecting and encouraging local production

Basic Concepts.text: Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are best described as
options: independent, often non-profit organizations that may support development initiatives
branches of government with statutory powers
private companies focused solely on profit maximization
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: independent, often non-profit organizations that may support development initiatives

Basic Concepts.text: NGOs contribute to agricultural development mainly through
options: training, funding and technical support to farmers
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: training, funding and technical support to farmers

Basic Concepts.text: IITA (International Institute of Tropical Agriculture) is an example of an international organization involved in
options: agricultural research and development in the tropics
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: agricultural research and development in the tropics

Basic Concepts.text: WARDA (West Africa Rice Development Association), now AfricaRice, focuses mainly on
options: rice research and development in West Africa
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: rice research and development in West Africa

Basic Concepts.text: ILCA (International Livestock Centre for Africa) was established mainly to focus on
options: livestock research and development in Africa
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: livestock research and development in Africa

Basic Concepts.text: ICRISAT (International Crop Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics) focuses on research into
options: crops suited to semi-arid tropical conditions, such as sorghum and millet
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: crops suited to semi-arid tropical conditions, such as sorghum and millet

Basic Concepts.text: NGOs assist farmers with microfinance mainly by
options: providing small loans and credit facilities to smallholder farmers
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: providing small loans and credit facilities to smallholder farmers

Basic Concepts.text: One advantage of NGO involvement in agriculture is that they often
options: complement government efforts, especially in underserved rural areas
compete negatively against government programmes with no benefit
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: complement government efforts, especially in underserved rural areas

Basic Concepts.text: NGOs may support agricultural development through provision of
options: training, farm inputs and market linkages Page 10 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: training, farm inputs and market linkages Page 10 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions

Basic Concepts.text: A key characteristic distinguishing NGOs from government agencies is that NGOs are typically
options: independent of direct government control, though they may collaborate with government
entirely controlled and funded solely by government
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: independent of direct government control, though they may collaborate with government

Basic Concepts.text: The Land Use Act in Nigeria was enacted mainly to
options: vest land ownership in state governments and ease land access for development
transfer all land to foreign investors
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: vest land ownership in state governments and ease land access for development

Basic Concepts.text: Traditional/communal land tenure systems in West Africa are characterized by
options: land being held collectively by families, clans or communities
land being owned exclusively by the central government
total absence of any land ownership concept
land being owned only by foreign corporations
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: land being held collectively by families, clans or communities

Basic Concepts.text: An advantage of the Land Use Act is that it
options: simplifies the process of land acquisition for development including agriculture
abolishes the concept of land ownership
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: simplifies the process of land acquisition for development including agriculture

Basic Concepts.text: A disadvantage associated with the Land Use Act is that it
options: may create bureaucratic delays in land allocation processes
eliminates all forms of bureaucracy instantly
guarantees immediate access to land for every citizen
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: may create bureaucratic delays in land allocation processes

Basic Concepts.text: Land reforms in West Africa are generally aimed at
options: improving equitable access to land and its productive use
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: improving equitable access to land and its productive use

Basic Concepts.text: Fragmentation of farmland due to inheritance practices under customary land tenure can lead to
options: reduced farm efficiency due to smaller, scattered plots Page 11 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
improved efficiency due to larger farm sizes
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: reduced farm efficiency due to smaller, scattered plots Page 11 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions

Basic Concepts.text: Leasehold tenure, as a land ownership arrangement, allows a person to
options: use land for a specified period under agreed terms with the landowner
own the land permanently with no conditions
use the land without any agreement
transfer government ownership to a private individual permanently
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: use land for a specified period under agreed terms with the landowner

Basic Concepts.text: Freehold land tenure grants the holder
options: absolute and permanent ownership rights over the land
no rights over the land at all
rights that expire after one growing season
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: absolute and permanent ownership rights over the land

Basic Concepts.text: One major aim of agricultural land reform is to
options: reduce insecurity of tenure and encourage long-term investment in land
eliminate customary land practices without any replacement system
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: reduce insecurity of tenure and encourage long-term investment in land

Basic Concepts.text: Government regulation of land use for agriculture versus other purposes (e.g. mining, housing) is necessary mainly to
options: balance competing land use needs and protect agricultural land
discourage any planning around land use
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: balance competing land use needs and protect agricultural land

Basic Concepts.text: Which of the following best explains why agriculture is regarded as the backbone of many West African economies?
options: It employs the majority of the population and contributes significantly to GDP
It has no measurable economic contribution
It is a purely recreational activity
It contributes nothing to industrial development
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: It employs the majority of the population and contributes significantly to GDP

Basic Concepts.text: The main aim of establishing colleges and universities of agriculture is to
options: train skilled manpower for agricultural research, extension and production
discourage the study of agricultural science
reduce the number of trained agriculturists
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: train skilled manpower for agricultural research, extension and production

Basic Concepts.text: A well-implemented agricultural policy should ideally aim to
options: balance the interests of producers, consumers and the environment
favour only urban consumers with no regard for farmers
discourage agricultural trade entirely Page 12 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: balance the interests of producers, consumers and the environment

Basic Concepts.text: Which of the following best describes "mixed farming" as a type of agriculture?
options: Combining crop production and livestock rearing on the same farm
Rearing only poultry with no crops
A method of soil conservation only
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: Combining crop production and livestock rearing on the same farm

Basic Concepts.text: Plantation agriculture typically involves
options: large-scale cultivation of a single cash crop such as rubber or oil palm
keeping a few animals in a backyard
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: large-scale cultivation of a single cash crop such as rubber or oil palm

Basic Concepts.text: The main goal of the National Accelerated Food Production Programme (NAFPP) was to
options: boost the production of staple food crops
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: boost the production of staple food crops

Basic Concepts.text: Bureaucratic delays in accessing government agricultural support are best classified as a problem of
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: agricultural administration and policy implementation

Basic Concepts.text: A key reason government establishes commodity marketing boards (historically) was to
options: regulate the marketing and pricing of export crops
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: regulate the marketing and pricing of export crops

Basic Concepts.text: Corruption and mismanagement of agricultural funds is a problem because it
options: diverts resources meant for farmers and reduces programme effectiveness
always improves farmers' access to resources
has no bearing on programme outcomes
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: diverts resources meant for farmers and reduces programme effectiveness

Basic Concepts.text: A key long-term solution to environmental degradation affecting agricultural land is
options: sustainable land management practices such as afforestation and erosion control
Basic Concepts.correct_answer: sustainable land management practices such as afforestation and erosion control

Agricultural Ecology.text: Agricultural ecology (agroecology) is best defined as the study of
options: the relationship between living organisms and their environment in farming systems
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: the relationship between living organisms and their environment in farming systems

Agricultural Ecology.text: An ecosystem is best described as
options: a community of living organisms interacting with their non-living environment
a single crop grown in isolation
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: a community of living organisms interacting with their non-living environment

Agricultural Ecology.text: The biotic components of a farm ecosystem include
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: plants, animals and micro-organisms

Agricultural Ecology.text: The abiotic components of a farm ecosystem include
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: temperature, rainfall, soil and light

Agricultural Ecology.text: In a mixed cropping system, the interaction where two crops mutually benefit each other is called
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: mutualism

Agricultural Ecology.text: Competition in an agro-ecosystem occurs when organisms
options: struggle for the same limited resources such as light, water and nutrients
have no relationship with each other
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: struggle for the same limited resources such as light, water and nutrients

Agricultural Ecology.text: An aquatic agro-ecosystem example is
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: a fish pond

Agricultural Ecology.text: A terrestrial agro-ecosystem example is
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: a crop farm on land

Agricultural Ecology.text: Understanding agro-ecology helps farmers to
options: manage farming systems sustainably by considering ecological interactions
ignore environmental factors in production decisions
focus solely on chemical inputs with no regard for ecology
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: manage farming systems sustainably by considering ecological interactions

Agricultural Ecology.text: Parasitism, as an ecological interaction, involves
options: one organism benefiting at the expense of another (the host)
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: one organism benefiting at the expense of another (the host)

Agricultural Ecology.text: Which of the following best describes symbiosis?
options: A close, often mutually beneficial relationship between two different organisms
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: A close, often mutually beneficial relationship between two different organisms

Agricultural Ecology.text: Rhizobium bacteria living in legume root nodules is an example of
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: mutualism (symbiosis)

Agricultural Ecology.text: In a mixed farming system combining crops and livestock, manure from animals benefits crops mainly by
options: having no effect on crop growth
eliminating the need for any nutrient management
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: improving soil fertility

Agricultural Ecology.text: Land, as a factor of production, can be defined as
options: all natural resources including soil, water bodies and minerals used in production
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: all natural resources including soil, water bodies and minerals used in production

Agricultural Ecology.text: A key characteristic of land is that it is Page 15 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
options: a free gift of nature and generally immobile
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: a free gift of nature and generally immobile

Agricultural Ecology.text: Land is described as "limited in supply" because
options: the total amount of land available cannot be increased indefinitely
more land can always be created at will
land quantity increases automatically with population growth
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: the total amount of land available cannot be increased indefinitely

Agricultural Ecology.text: Which of the following is an agricultural use of land?
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: Crop production

Agricultural Ecology.text: Which of the following is a non-agricultural use of land?
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: Industrial site development

Agricultural Ecology.text: Game reserves and wildlife conservation areas represent land used mainly for
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: wildlife/game conservation, an agricultural-related use

Agricultural Ecology.text: Land used for livestock production is an example of
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: agricultural land use

Agricultural Ecology.text: Immobility, as a characteristic of land, means that
options: land cannot be physically moved from one location to another
land can be transported like machinery
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: land cannot be physically moved from one location to another

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil type is a physical factor affecting land availability for agriculture because
options: some soils are more suited to crop production than others
soil type has no bearing on land suitability Page 16 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
all soils are equally suitable for every crop
soil type only matters for building construction
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: some soils are more suited to crop production than others

Agricultural Ecology.text: Topography, as a physical factor, affects agricultural land use mainly through
options: slope and terrain influencing erosion risk and mechanization potential
having no effect on farming decisions
determining only the market price of produce
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: slope and terrain influencing erosion risk and mechanization potential

Agricultural Ecology.text: Land degradation reduces land available for agriculture mainly by
options: reducing soil fertility and productive capacity
having no effect on land productivity
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: reducing soil fertility and productive capacity

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil pollution, as a physical factor, limits agricultural land availability by
options: introducing harmful substances that reduce soil productivity
having no effect on crop growth
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: introducing harmful substances that reduce soil productivity

Agricultural Ecology.text: Population pressure, as an economic factor, affects land availability for agriculture by
options: increasing competition for land for housing and other uses
reducing the demand for agricultural land
having no effect on land use patterns
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: increasing competition for land for housing and other uses

Agricultural Ecology.text: Expansion of industries reduces land available for agriculture mainly because
options: industrial land use competes with agricultural land use
industries are always built on water bodies only
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: industrial land use competes with agricultural land use

Agricultural Ecology.text: Mining and mineral exploitation can reduce agricultural land availability by
options: converting farmland to mining sites and causing land degradation
improving soil fertility of mined areas immediately
having no impact on agricultural land use
always increasing crop yield in mined areas
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: converting farmland to mining sites and causing land degradation

Agricultural Ecology.text: Recreation and tourism development can affect agricultural land availability by
options: converting farmland into recreational facilities such as resorts and parks
having no effect on land use
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: converting farmland into recreational facilities such as resorts and parks

Agricultural Ecology.text: Land tenure system, as a socio-cultural factor, affects agricultural land availability mainly through
options: traditional ownership practices influencing access and security of land use
having no bearing on farmers' access to land
eliminating the need for any land use planning
guaranteeing unlimited free land to all farmers
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: traditional ownership practices influencing access and security of land use

Agricultural Ecology.text: Religious land uses (e.g., churches, mosques, shrines) reduce land available for agriculture because
options: such land is set aside for spiritual/cultural purposes rather than farming
religious institutions never occupy any land
such land automatically becomes farmland after use
this factor has no relevance to land availability
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: such land is set aside for spiritual/cultural purposes rather than farming

Agricultural Ecology.text: The paper industry relies mainly on which agricultural raw material?
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: Pulpwood

Agricultural Ecology.text: The beverage industry relies mainly on agricultural raw materials such as
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: cocoa and tea

Agricultural Ecology.text: The textile industry relies mainly on the agricultural raw material
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: cotton

Agricultural Ecology.text: The soap and cosmetics industry relies mainly on
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: vegetable oils and oil seeds

Agricultural Ecology.text: The leather industry depends mainly on
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: hides and skins from livestock

Agricultural Ecology.text: The canning industry commonly uses agricultural raw materials such as
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: meat and fish

Agricultural Ecology.text: One way agriculture supports industries is by
options: providing raw materials for agro-based manufacturing
competing directly against all industries with no linkage
reducing the supply of industrial inputs
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: providing raw materials for agro-based manufacturing

Agricultural Ecology.text: One way industry supports agriculture is by
options: providing farm machinery, chemicals and processing equipment
discouraging the use of any farm inputs
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: providing farm machinery, chemicals and processing equipment

Agricultural Ecology.text: Agriculture provides a market for industrial products such as
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: farm machinery and agrochemicals

Agricultural Ecology.text: Agriculture supports industrial workers mainly by
options: providing food to sustain the industrial workforce
having no linkage with industrial labour
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: providing food to sustain the industrial workforce

Agricultural Ecology.text: Rainfall, as a climatic factor, mainly affects crop production through its influence on
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: water availability for plant growth

Agricultural Ecology.text: Temperature affects both crop and animal production mainly by influencing
options: metabolic processes, growth rates and geographic suitability of species
only the price of farm produce
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: metabolic processes, growth rates and geographic suitability of species

Agricultural Ecology.text: Light, as a climatic factor, is essential for crop production mainly because it is required for Page 19 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: photosynthesis

Agricultural Ecology.text: Wind, as a climatic factor, can affect crop production by causing
options: lodging of crops and aiding pollination/seed dispersal
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: lodging of crops and aiding pollination/seed dispersal

Agricultural Ecology.text: Relative humidity affects agricultural production mainly by influencing
options: the incidence of pests and diseases
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: the incidence of pests and diseases

Agricultural Ecology.text: Predators, as a biotic factor, affect agricultural production by
options: preying on pests or, in some cases, on livestock
always improving crop yield with no downside
having no effect on farm animals
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: preying on pests or, in some cases, on livestock

Agricultural Ecology.text: Parasites, as a biotic factor, affect production mainly by
options: living on or in a host organism and causing harm
having no impact on host health
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: living on or in a host organism and causing harm

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil micro-organisms, as a biotic factor, can be beneficial to agriculture by
options: decomposing organic matter and fixing nitrogen
having no role in nutrient cycling
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: decomposing organic matter and fixing nitrogen

Agricultural Ecology.text: Pathogens, as a biotic factor, are organisms that
options: cause disease in crops or animals
have no effect on agricultural production
are only found in soil, never in water
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: cause disease in crops or animals

Agricultural Ecology.text: Weeds, as a biotic factor, affect crop production mainly by
options: competing with crops for light, water, and nutrients
having no effect on crop growth
eliminating the need for soil nutrients Page 20 WAEC Agricultural Science — 1000 Practice Questions
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: competing with crops for light, water, and nutrients

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil pH, as an edaphic factor, affects crop production mainly by influencing
options: the availability of nutrients to plants
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: the availability of nutrients to plants

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil texture, as an edaphic factor, affects crop production mainly through its influence on
options: water retention and aeration of the soil
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: water retention and aeration of the soil

Agricultural Ecology.text: Soil structure, as an edaphic factor, affects plant growth mainly by influencing
options: root penetration, aeration and water movement
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: root penetration, aeration and water movement

Agricultural Ecology.text: Which of the following best illustrates mutualism between two biotic components of a farm ecosystem?
options: Rhizobium bacteria and leguminous plant roots
A weed competing with a crop for nutrients
A pathogen causing disease in livestock
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: Rhizobium bacteria and leguminous plant roots

Agricultural Ecology.text: Igneous rocks are formed through
options: cooling and solidification of molten magma
transformation of existing rocks by heat and pressure
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: cooling and solidification of molten magma

Agricultural Ecology.text: Sedimentary rocks are formed mainly through
options: compaction and cementation of deposited sediments
Agricultural Ecology.correct_answer: compaction and cementation of deposited sediments

Agricultural Ecology.text: Metamorphic rocks are formed when existing rocks undergo
options: transformation due to intense heat and/or pressure
